pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: Walk me through your Tracker type: what state does it hold, why did you pick that representation, and how do structs, slices, maps, and methods each show up in your design?
expected_points: Task is a struct grouping id, title, done; Tracker holds tasks in a slice to keep insertion order
methods on *Tracker (pointer receiver) so Add/Complete mutate the real state, not a copy
a map appears in Summary (and possibly elsewhere); learner can say why the main store is a slice, not a map (order)

questions.prompt: Your program starts by loading tracker.txt. What happens when the file is missing, and what happens when a line is garbage? How does errors.Is still recognize your corrupt-file error after you wrapped it?
expected_points: missing file is not an error: detected with errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist), Load returns an empty tracker
a bad line fails with an error wrapping the ErrCorrupt sentinel and naming the line number
fmt.Errorf with %w keeps the sentinel in the error chain, and errors.Is walks that chain

questions.prompt: Trace `go run . complete 2` from the shell to the updated file: where do the words 'complete' and '2' come from, and which functions run in what order?
expected_points: os.Args carries the arguments; os.Args[0] is the program name, the rest go to dispatch
dispatch switches on the subcommand and converts "2" with strconv.Atoi
main sequences it: Load, dispatch (which calls Complete), Save, print — errors go to stderr with exit 1

questions.prompt: You added your own table-driven test. What did you test, and what does the table style buy you over writing a separate test function per case?
expected_points: learner can describe their own test and why the cases differ meaningfully
one assertion body, many cases: adding a case is one struct literal, not copy-pasted logic
t.Run gives each case a name so failures point at the exact input

questions.prompt: Why does the tracker logic live in its own package instead of package main? What rule decided which identifiers got capital letters?
expected_points: tracker never prints or reads os.Args, so its logic is testable and reusable; main stays a thin shell
exported (capitalized) names are the package's public API — Task, Add, ErrNotFound; internals stay lowercase
echoes hello-world's Greeting-vs-main split at project scale

questions.prompt: List returns a copy of the task slice. What could go wrong if it returned the internal slice directly?
expected_points: slices share their backing array, so the caller could mutate the tracker's own data without calling any method
the copy keeps every state change flowing through Add/Complete, where the invariants live

questions.prompt: Two terminals run your tracker at the same moment. What can happen to tracker.txt, and why can't your current code prevent it?
expected_points: both load the same state, both save, last write wins — one terminal's change is silently lost
the program has no coordination between processes; recognizing the gap is enough — solutions come in later stages
